result.notes: Ramp has a substantial official REST API (docs.ramp.com/developer-api, api.ramp.com/developer/v1) covering transactions, cards, bills, vendors, reimbursements, purchase orders, trips, accounting sync (Accounting API alone has ~45-50 endpoints per OpenAPI spec sampling; Composio's toolkit wraps 88 tools). Auth is OAuth2 only: a business Admin/Business Owner creates a "Developer app" in-app and enables the client_credentials grant for server-to-server access to their own data (self-serve within an existing paid Ramp business account); authorization_code/OAuth is used when onboarding other businesses. Building an integration that serves OTHER Ramp businesses (the agent-toolkit case) requires either the sandbox access form (self-serve, ~1 min provisioning, pre-populated sandbox business) for testing, then explicitly "apply for production access," or going through Ramp's Technology Partner Program (contact-sales form) for embedded/integration partnerships - hence partner_gated/yellow rather than fully self-serve. Notably Ramp also ships an OFFICIAL hosted MCP server (mcp.ramp.com/mcp, one-click install for Claude/ChatGPT) that proxies the authenticated end-user's own Ramp permissions - this is a strong, low-friction path for an agent toolkit even though the raw REST API has partner gating for multi-tenant production use. api_breadth marked "large" with moderate confidence only - could not get an exact total endpoint count within budget (OpenAPI spec fetch was truncated to the Accounting sub-API).
result.one_liner: Ramp is a corporate card, expense management, bill pay, and accounting-automation platform for businesses, with a developer REST API and an official hosted MCP server for AI agents.
